title: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
seo_title: Measures of Central Tendency – JSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the mean, median and mode of ungrouped and grouped data; find the range; compare data sets. (summary of the NERDC JSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 maths worksheets on averages: mean, median and mode from frequency tables, estimated mean of grouped data, missing values and comparing data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Grouped data: use the class mid-points.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Mean from a table = Σfx ÷ Σf.
  • For grouped data, use the mid-point of each class as x. The answer is an estimate.
  • The median is the middle value; the mode is the most common value; the range is highest − lowest.

Examples

Example

Classes 10–19 (f 4), 20–29 (f 6)

Mid-points 14.5 and 24.5

(58 + 147) ÷ 10

Answer: Estimated mean 20.5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using class limits instead of mid-pointsUse the mid-point.
Dividing by the number of classesDivide by Σf.
Thinking the estimate is exactGrouped data gives an estimate.

faq.q: Why is the grouped mean an estimate?
faq.a: We do not know the exact values in each class.
The class with the highest frequency.
